Homemates production retest

8 November 2026 · Live app · Release eead9d1

All six reported issues passed the five-household regression test. The run used the original QA household records in production, independent Firebase email sign-ins and separate Chromium storage for a desktop viewport (1280 × 850) and a mobile touch viewport (390 × 844). Both sessions used the owner account. Cash requests were submitted through the owner’s staff preview. Browser opened the deployed Today screen independently. The paired sessions ran with Playwright.

What actually saved

  • Photos. Each of the five supplied JPEGs was resized and saved with its staff record in Postgres. On the mobile session the saved value matched the rendered source byte for byte and decoded to a 384 × 384 image. Older browser-only photo addresses need a fresh upload. The five original QA photos were re-uploaded.
  • Tasks. Each newly created assignment had one row, the expected staff member, completed status and a completion timestamp. The second browser saw the change without reloading.
  • Attendance and payroll. Each directory hire had both a payroll profile and a draft run. For the five original ₹12,000 staff salaries, a confirmed absence deducted ₹400. On the second browser the payroll screen and the downloaded Excel workbook both showed ₹11,600. Correcting the date to present restored ₹12,000 in Postgres. The calculation uses the existing 30-day basis and rounds the daily amount up. The QA payroll runs were drafts.
  • Purchases. Each ₹47 request was approved, posted, linked to its expense and inventory item, and recorded one movement of two units. All five starting quantities moved from 4 to 6. A separate Cedar retry test added one more unit. Inventory tracking requires selecting an existing stock item and entering its quantity. Expense-only purchases can be posted separately.
  • Languages. All five language choices survived reload and matched the account preference stored in Postgres. In an additional Cedar run the same household switched through all five languages, reopened Tasks and checked the heading from the other browser each time.
  • Categories. I submitted each manual expense without selecting a category. The form stayed open and asked for a category. After selection there was one ₹23 expense with the chosen category in Postgres. The category and stock actions were independent.

Retry and history checks

A purchase using a stock item from another QA household rolled back. The request remained approved and no expense was created. Two concurrent submissions of the corrected request produced one expense, one movement and one added unit. For a ₹6,000 relief worker with a ₹25 manual deduction, recording absence twice produced ₹5,775 net. Reversing it restored ₹5,975 and preserved the manual deduction.

I corrected the four known QA expenses that had defaulted to Fuel. The original driver’s fuel purchase retained Fuel. I also linked Maple Garden’s old ₹65 seedling-tray request to its matching expense after confirming household, staff, amount, description and timestamps. The original purchase had no recorded stock quantity, so it has no reconstructed inventory movement.

Production profile screenshots

Release and coverage

Firebase SQL Connect and Cloud SQL migrations were deployed to homemates-d23bc. The GitHub main branch deployed to the production Vercel alias. The initial connector failed on live SQL execution during payroll setup. After moving the dependent writes into PostgreSQL transactions and redeploying, the Today screen recovered and the household checks passed. The project’s 29 unit tests, TypeScript and production build passed.

The two devices were simulated browsers on one computer. Physical phones, NFC hardware, Telegram recipient delivery, staff-account authorization and Google OAuth were outside this six-issue retest. The tests used fictional QA records. Historical expenses or broken photo references in other households were not reclassified or reconstructed.
